subject.title: [Bug]: Codex OAuth refresh succeeds but cron/heartbeat fail with 10s auth refresh timeout

question: Should OpenClaw mitigate Codex's fixed 10-second external-auth callback for still-valid ChatGPT OAuth tokens, or wait for upstream Codex to make that timeout configurable?
rationale: The source gap crosses OpenClaw's auth-profile policy and upstream Codex's external-auth RPC contract; increasing timeouts, reusing cached tokens, or waiting for upstream each has different auth freshness and compatibility tradeoffs.

options.title: Mitigate in OpenClaw with cached valid tokens
options.body: Use the existing valid access token for Codex app-server refresh callbacks when it is not near expiry, and reserve forced refresh for expired or unauthorized states with the current reauth error path.

options.title: Wait for upstream Codex configurability
options.body: Keep this issue open but do not change OpenClaw until upstream Codex exposes a configurable or longer external-auth refresh deadline.

options.title: Fold into broader auth incident design
options.body: Move the remaining behavior into the broader provider quarantine/status work if maintainers want one policy to cover timeout, invalidated-token, and wedged-lane cases together.

recommendation.title: Mitigate in OpenClaw with cached valid tokens
recommendation.body: Use the existing valid access token for Codex app-server refresh callbacks when it is not near expiry, and reserve forced refresh for expired or unauthorized states with the current reauth error path.
